finding.statement: A run of further English parish, probate, and muster records clears or bounds the remaining same-name field. Two burials place a continuing English John-and-Mary household well past the emigrant's own death: at St Mary, Harrow on the Hill, Middlesex, a John and Mary Gurney 'of Okington' buried a daughter Ann on 30 January 1669 and a son Isaac on 8 February 1669. At Toddington, Bedfordshire, John Gurney (married Elizabeth Moreton there in 1624) was himself buried in September 1641, three months after the colonial John's Weymouth fine and twenty-one years before the Braintree John's 1662/3 death. A third London burial, of 'John sonne of ffrancis Garney Joyner' at St Giles Cripplegate in December 1640, documents a third, trade-distinct Cripplegate-area Garney/Gurney family. A dozen further Prerogative Court of Canterbury probate records anchor separate English clusters kept apart from Candidates A and C: Anne Gurney, widow of Eythorne, Kent (will 1656); Daniel Gurney of Aylesbury (will 1669, naming a brother John) and a probate sentence for a further Aylesbury John; William Gurney of London (will 1655, sons John, Abel, Walter); Richard Gurney, a London labourer (will 1674/5); and Sir Richard Gurney together with the 1577 Tobias/Edward Gurney wills, both too early or unrelated to the Norfolk family. The 1641-42 Protestation Returns add a final negative: the surviving Buckinghamshire returns name several Gurneys at Stewkley and neighbouring parishes but no John anywhere, consistent with Candidate A having already moved into Northamptonshire by 1641.

limitations: FamilySearch's cross-collection index does not cover every English parish register or non-conformist record, so an unindexed Richard or Isaac baptism could exist outside this search.
The search filtered to entries tagged 'Principal' for the baptized child; a mis-tagged or mis-indexed entry naming father John could have been missed.

finding.shortLabel: No English John Gurney household outside the named candidates carries a Richard, John Jr., Peter, or Isaac

sources.locator: Cluster-anchor searches for Richard Gurney (father John, 1620-1645, 388 results reviewed) and Isaac Gurney (father John, 1620-1650, 287 results reviewed), 2026-05-11

finding.statement: A search anchored on the colonial John's two rarest children's names -- Richard and Isaac -- across every English collection FamilySearch indexes returns exactly one Richard Gurney baptism with a father named John (Richard Gurnie, baptized 15 December 1626, St Peter, Hertfordshire -- Candidate C's own already-eliminated Richard) and zero Isaac Gurney baptisms with a father named John. No English John Gurney household anywhere, outside the candidates already named, carries a Richard, a John Jr., a Peter, or an Isaac in any combination. This is not treated as a definitive elimination on its own: it is equally consistent with the colonial John fathering his distinctive children entirely in Massachusetts after his June 1641 emigration, which is what the colonial record in fact shows.
